QF.id: Cat III AIF Fees and Performance_15

question.text: A low hurdle rate is generally preferred by:

answer.text: Investors, as they get higher accrued returns
The Investment Manager, as it enables higher incentive fees

explanation.text: The Logic: The workbook states that the Investment Manager prefers a low hurdle rate because it is easier to clear and therefore generates higher incentive fees, while investors prefer a high hurdle rate because more of the fund's return then accrues to them as preferred return. The Trap: A high hurdle reduces annual incentive-fee eligibility, so it is investors — not managers — who benefit from raising it. SEBI and trustees do not set the hurdle for commercial preference reasons. Note: The manager-vs-investor preference around hurdle rate is from the AIF (Category III) Distributors workbook (Series XIX-B).
